title: ～だけで — “just by ～ / with only ～”
summary: だけで means that one small thing alone is enough to bring about a result: ‘just by ～ing’. It follows a verb or noun, and the result clause shows how much that small thing achieves. It often expresses surprise or a feeling.

patterns.gloss: plain form + だけで (見るだけで)
noun + だけで (名前だけで)

body.p: Use the plain form of the verb (dictionary or past) or a noun, then だけで: 写真を見るだけで, 名前を聞いただけで. After that comes the result.
だけ means ‘only’, and で marks the means or cause. Together: ‘with just that, ...’. The small action may be dictionary form (general) or past form (a specific event).
だけ alone limits something (水だけ飲む, ‘drink only water’). だけで adds a cause-and-result link: even this alone is enough to make something happen. The result is often a feeling or understanding.

examples.ja: 名前（なまえ）を聞（き）いただけで、すぐ分（わ）かりました。
examples.romaji: Namae o kiita dake de, sugu wakarimashita.
examples.tr: Just by hearing the name, I understood right away.
examples.note: Past form 聞いた + だけで for a specific event.

examples.ja: 写真（しゃしん）を見（み）るだけで、楽（たの）しくなる。
examples.romaji: Shashin o miru dake de, tanoshiku naru.
examples.tr: Just by looking at the photos, I feel happy.
examples.note: Dictionary form for a general feeling.

examples.ja: 話（はなし）を聞（き）くだけで、答（こた）えが分（わ）かった。
examples.romaji: Hanashi o kiku dake de, kotae ga wakatta.
examples.tr: Just by listening to the story, I understood the answer.
examples.note: A small effort leads to understanding.

pitfalls: Don't confuse だけで with だけ alone (which only limits). だけで needs a result clause.
A noun takes だけで directly: 名前だけで, not 名前のだけで.
